before.label: baseline
limitations: Synthetic rubric and response probabilities are authored hypotheses, not real candidate/expert labels.
Virtual profiles are repeated seeds of four ability prototypes across six roles, not independent expert assessments.
Answer generation uses independent probability tables, not the product Rasch model.
Retests use independent answer draws and different variants; variants can overlap in question families across attempts.
Holdout separates specialization/scenario families and forms; it shares the same authored response model and is not an independent human population.
No source code is executed; coding responses simulate trusted judge snapshots.
Item discrimination here measures the simulator, not empirical question-bank validity.
